source_evidence.observation: The text takes the central limit theorem special case of Bernoulli variables with one fixed p in (0,1).
A Ber(p) variable is 1 or 0 with probabilities p and 1-p, has mean p and variance p(1-p), and S_N is Binom(N,p).
As N tends to infinity, (S_N-Np)/sqrt(Np(1-p)) converges to N(0,1) in distribution.
This Bernoulli special case is named the de Moivre-Laplace theorem.
